recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not restore the old core ShareableLibrary profile; future ShareableLibrary profile maintenance should occur in CRMI unless a new work-group decision brings the profile family back into core.
issue_request: FHIR-18228 was Published/Persuasive for STU3 and asked core FHIR to define a ShareableLibrary profile, analogous to ShareableValueSet, with url, version, name, title, experimental, description, date, and publisher as publishing metadata requirements.
initial_application: Commit 421cbd47bd4326f440463b84dc4c7f27a5360a9b applied the issue by adding source/library/library-shareable-spreadsheet.xml and registering Shareable Library in source/library/library-spreadsheet.xml. Historical R4/R4B/R5 artifacts include StructureDefinition/shareablelibrary, and later converted source retained source/library/structuredefinition-profile-shareablelibrary.xml until R6 removal work.
additional_context: FHIR-48393 was Applied/Persuasive for R6 and explicitly removed ShareableLibrary and related resource profiles from the base specification because they had moved to CRMI or other external IGs. Current Clinical Reasoning and Shareable pattern source directs applications to CRMI for Shareable, Publishable, Computable, and Executable profiles, and published CRMI exposes an active CRMI Shareable Library profile.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Recreating StructureDefinition/shareablelibrary in core would reverse FHIR-48393 and conflict with the current build scope, where Library remains active but Library profile pack entries are intentionally absent. The remaining core OID row is historical identifier metadata, not an active profile definition.

related_jiras.note: Applied R6 CDS decision removed ShareableLibrary and sibling resource profiles from core after they moved to CRMI or other external IGs.
Later Library profile additions were audited separately and are likewise governed for current core by FHIR-48393.
Later Library profile replacement work was audited separately and is likewise governed for current core by FHIR-48393.
